Gives the evidence hierarchy for the image/trust decision.

title: How Users Actually Read Websites
why: Summary of NN/g eye-tracking (F, layer-cake, spotted and commitment patterns). Inline elements such as block quotes and tables draw fixations but switch readers from reading to scanning. NN/g's concise + scannable + objective rewrite showed +124% usability. Front-load each paragraph; the 'zoom out and read only the headers' test. Evidence base for designing articles that aren't walls of text.

title: How To Build a Website SO Premium They Beg You To Buy
why: Says #1 premium signal is bespoke assets: 'most cheap websites are just text' plus stock photos; custom graphics that break up content and guide the eye, but only if they match the brand (an off-brand graphic is worse than none). Also cohesive palette/fonts, subtle motion (not bouncing), and a clear site structure for SEO. Agency funnel (checklist/booking).

title: Designing for Trust - Margot Bloomstein, Author of Trustworthy
why: Respected content strategist (book 'Trustworthy') on building trust through content and design consistency and giving the audience 'enough' information to decide confidently. Useful for blog trust strategy beyond visuals.

title: The Psychology of Premium Websites
why: Framework: ~50 ms first impression and halo effect (hero and cover image quality colour everything after), cognitive fluency (whitespace, hierarchy), peak-end rule via micro-interactions; uses Apple, Hermès/Bottega and Stripe as examples. Good for prioritising article hero/cover quality.

title: I Studied 1,000 Websites, Here's What Works in 2026
why: Counterweight: clarity beats aesthetics, and social proof beats design ('if I had to choose one, trust signals'). Restraint in motion (luxury sites let things breathe); micro-details like custom badges signal care. For us: only REAL proof (no fake reviews per taboo).

title: How to Avoid AI Slop in Vibe-Coded Landing Pages
why: From a respected design-education channel: identify the typical AI mistakes and prompt them away iteratively. A complement to Impeccable for auditing our Next.js pages against 2026 'AI-made' tells.

title: How I design websites with EDITORIAL style layouts (part 2)
why: Translating editorial layouts to mobile in Figma plus developer handoff. Rebuts 'editorial = form over function': hierarchy via type, spacing and composition guides the eye. Relevant since our audience is mobile-first.

title: How to Fix AI Slop with CLAUDE DESIGN
why: Five fixes for the AI look: an inspiration board, dropping the Inter font, giving every colour a job, breaking the centred layout, and real images/video. About 22.9K views. Popular tooling video with an affiliate funnel (Higgsfield), so lower authority, but recent. ID taken from a mirror URL (divert.stream/watch/S2DE95bGld0).

title: Brand Photography Trends that will DOMINATE in 2026
why: Premium brand-photo direction for 2026: UGC-style, spur-of-the-moment compositions (even iPhone frames shot on set), and motifs 'one level deeper' instead of literal props (no laptop+coffee). Movement and short video clips are expected. Maps well to a 'model's own profile' aesthetic for article imagery.

title: 6 INSANE Website Design Tricks Luxury Brands Use
why: Concrete premium-imagery rule: quality + consistency + uniform colour grading across all images (mismatched sizes and grades cheapen a page). Also: wordmark logos, black/white base, alignment, and telling your story with 'physical evidence' because a new brand must answer 'can I trust you?'. Don't copy Chanel, which has existing demand. Marketing-agency channel.

title: Website Conversion Strategy: Irwin Hau on Proof Density in the AI Era
why: Concept of 'proof density': in an AI era where testimonials are easy to fake, trust needs several layered proofs across the site, not one block. Notes the site is checked by job candidates too (recruitment). 24-minute interview, about 70K sites analysed (claim).

title: Website Design Secrets: Make Your Site Look Expensive
why: Older but the most specific on photo choice: candid, unposed, off-angle, unusual crops look more high-end than staged straight-on shots. Avoid overused free stock; if an image doesn't add to the look, use whitespace instead. Don't write 'luxury' in copy; one deliberate rule-break only.

title: The Rise of Lo-Fi Content: Authenticity in Post Aesthetics
why: Lo-fi or 'phone' aesthetic only converts if it is still branded, strategic and pretty ('you on your best day off'). Recommends a high-low mix (casual image + polished frame). A guardrail for a selfie-style visual direction so it doesn't look cheap.
